text:
Maria G.: Heads-up — we need a bump in public IP capacity for the new GPU onboarding in eu-west-1.
We plan to spin up 40 new dedicated GPU nodes that each need 2 public IPs (control + debug), plus we want room for autoscale and failover. Current limit is 5 Elastic IPs per region. Can someone start a quota request?

Todd: Ack. Can you post the exact numbers you want? Also, do we actually need EIPs for all nodes or can we NAT?

Maria G.: Numbers: request Elastic IP quota -> 80 (we're asking for headroom), ENI limit increase -> allow 400 total ENIs, secondary private IPs per ENI -> increase to 50, VPC CIDR / subnet size looked ok but we might need a larger number of available private IPs across worker subnets (requesting guidance).
We need IPv6 enabled on the VPCs for future-proofing — request Amazon-provided IPv6 block for that VPC.

Jen L.: TL;DR: +80 EIPs, ENIs to 400, secondary IPs 50/eni, enable IPv6. Please include: account-id 123456789012 and the VPC IDs (vpc-0a1b2c3d). Put cost justification: production GPU fleet for customers, SLA-backed dedicated pools, can't reuse NAT for debug access because some customers require static endpoints for firewall allow-lists.

Maria G.: Adding the support justification in the request now. Also flagging that some of our telemetry and access tooling expects stable public IPs (we can move telemetry to relay later but that takes time).

Kevin: One minor ask — mark these EIPs as non-Elastic-File-Allocation (i.e., standard EIP) and add tags: Project=DedicatedGPU, Env=prod. Ops needs tags for chargeback.

InfraBot: Deploy-note: gpu-cluster-provisioner triggered validation, failed due to EIP quota during dry-run. -> log snippet: `ERROR: allocate_eip() -> QuotaExceeded: AddressLimitExceeded: You have reached the limit of Elastic IP addresses`

Maria G.: I've opened an AWS support case and provided the numbers + account details. Case ID: 1234567890. Please reference that in any internal followups.

AWS Support: Hello — we received case 1234567890. Asking for quota increases: Elastic IPs to 80, Network interfaces to 400, Secondary private IPs per ENI to 50, and enabling IPv6 for vpc-0a1b2c3d in eu-west-1. We've put it into a standard quota review and requested capacity verification. We'll update within 24-48 hours.

Todd: Thanks. If AWS pushes back on EIP count, fallback plan: use an allocated IPv4 prefix (bring-your-own-ip or request a /27 pool) or move debug endpoints behind an internal bastion + NAT that uses fewer public IPs. Can infra owners run quick feasibility?

Jen L.: Agreed. Also ask AWS to consider increasing VPC elastic network interface quota per ENI family — some of our inference nodes need lots of secondary IPs for sidecars.

Maria G.: Added that note to the case. I also included a short cost note: EIPs are free while attached, but running NAT gateways to reduce EIP use increases monthly cost. For a rough calc: 40 EIPs attached ~ no additional EIP cost, NAT gateway ~ $32/month + bandwidth per gateway, and adds latency/maintenance. Customers prefer fixed IPs.

Kevin: I'll prep a brief internal cost tradeoff doc so engineering leadership can sign off if we need to pay for static IPs vs re-architecting.

AWS Support: Update: we've approved Network Interfaces -> 400 and Secondary IPs per ENI -> 50. Elastic IP increase is pending further verification — AWS asked for a brief justification of why NAT gateways won't suffice and whether you can accept an IPv4 prefix instead. Please reply in the case.

Maria G.: Reply sent — explained customer firewall requirements and timeline. Also asked if AWS can allocate an IPv4 prefix (/26) as an alternative.

Todd: Good. Meanwhile, short-term mitigation: de-prioritize debug EIP assignment during autoscale and reuse a small pool of EIPs for ephemeral debug sessions (we need automation to rotate IP-to-node mappings). Can someone add a task?

Jen L.: Created a quick ticket in infra backlog: INFRA-4123 \"ephemeral-eip-pool-provisioner\". Owner: Kevin. ETA: two weeks.

Kevin: On it. I'll implement a small pool + NAT fallback and add tagging automation.

InfraBot: Reminder: re-run provisioner dry-run after increases are live.

Maria G.: Thanks all — marking this thread solved for now. Will post the finalized AWS case resolution once EIP is approved or we get prefix offer. :thumbsup:

Kevin: Ping me if you need the cost doc early.

AWS Support: Final: we've offered a /26 IPv4 prefix allocation to your account in eu-west-1 as an alternative to raising the per-account EIP limit. If you accept the prefix we can associate that to your VPCs and you can allocate addresses without consuming EIP quotas. Please confirm acceptance in the support case.

Maria G.: Accepting the /26 IPv4 prefix. Thanks AWS. We'll update provisioning to allocate from the prefix and keep tags.

Todd: Nice. That should reduce friction long-term.

Jen L.: Closing loop: INFRA-4123 linked to the provisioner changes so we can still handle ephemeral cases while we migrate to the prefix.

Maria G.: End of thread — case 1234567890 resolved with prefix allocation and quotas increased for ENIs/secondary IPs. Keep an eye on rollout next week.
